messages:
sara: Heads-up — just ran `terraform apply` in staging and it failed due to a lock. Plan afterwards shows the redis cluster as `tainted` and kube secret mismatch. Anyone seen this pattern before?

yusuf: saw similar yesterday after an interrupted apply. Backend is S3 + DynamoDB lock?

sara: yes S3 backend, dynamodb lock table in us-west-2. error was `Error locking state: ConditionalCheckFailedException`

lee: if it was an interrupted apply the usual is a stale lock row in Dynamo. You can do `terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID>` but be careful if an apply is actually still running. ops-bot should show recent locks.

ops-bot: recent-locks: 1) lock-id: abcd1234 user: cicd-runner started: 2026-03-08T17:12:03Z status: active 2) lock-id: zxy9-001 user: sara started: 2026-03-09T09:03:10Z status: orphaned

katie: @sara can you paste the exact `terraform plan` snippet that shows tainted redis?

sara: sure, pasted output below:
```
# module/databases.aws_elasticache_cluster.redis_cluster will be replaced
-/+ resource "aws_elasticache_cluster" "redis_cluster" {
    ~ id = "red-001" -> (known after apply)
      cluster_id = "red-001"
      node_type  = "cache.r6g.large"
      // (other attributes)
  }
```

yusuf: plan showing `-/+` means Terraform thinks it's going to recreate. Could be drift (manual change in console) or provider version weirdness. Any recent provider bumps in the PRs?

sara: we did merge #452 which bumped aws provider from 4.62 -> 4.74 in staging plan job yesterday.

lee: that provider bump could change defaulted attributes. Also kube secret mismatch — are we projecting the secret into k8s using external-secrets? If the secret key changed shape, plan may try to update the k8s manifest which in turn taints resources.

katie: quick check: run `terraform state show module.databases.aws_elasticache_cluster.redis_cluster` and compare attributes to console. If state doesn't match actual, we might import/reconcile or accept replacement.

sara: ran state show, found `parameter_group_name` different from console (console has red-redis-param-v2). Not sure when that changed.

yusuf: OK that explains recreate. If config is supposed to be v2 then update tf code to match and run `terraform import`? Actually import won't change computed diffs; import only sets tf state to match resource identity. You probably want to update the TF config to reflect the new parameter group and then run plan.

lee: also check drift for the kube secret: `kubectl get secret redis-creds -n staging -o yaml` vs what our k8s manifest in repo defines. If external-secrets is managing it, check the external-secrets controller logs.

sara: external-secrets shows reconcile OK, but secret length/encoding changed (base64 vs plain). I think ops changed the secret encoding when rotating creds.

katie: For the stale Dynamo lock: if ops-bot shows `orphaned` you can `terraform force-unlock zxy9-001` after confirming no active apply. Who's currently running CI?

ops-bot: active-applies: none in the last 30m. last successful apply: pipeline #782 by ci-runner at 2026-03-09T08:58:41Z

sara: OK I'm going to force-unlock and re-run plan. Will also open a quick PR to pin param group to v2 in TF. cc @yusuf for review.

yusuf: thanks — if you want to avoid recreate, update tf to the console value AND run `terraform import module.databases.aws_elasticache_cluster.redis_cluster red-001` to align state, then `terraform plan` should show no replace.

sara: doing import now. command: `terraform import -var-file=staging.tfvars module.databases.aws_elasticache_cluster.redis_cluster red-001`

lee: after import, `terraform plan -target=module.databases.aws_elasticache_cluster.redis_cluster` to verify. If plan still wants recreate, check provider changelog for attribute renames.

sara: import succeeded. plan now shows only a k8s secret update (encoding). Patch that in the manifest to keep base64 encoded.

katie: nice. For the taint bit: did you need to `terraform taint` anything manually?

sara: no manual tainting needed after import. The tainted marker disappeared.

yusuf: great — what's the final status for staging apply?

sara: I force-unlocked zxy9-001, imported redis, updated TF to param-v2, fixed k8s secret encoding in repo, opened PR <https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/478|PR #478> for the secret fix, and re-run `terraform apply` — apply completed successfully.

lee: awesome, thanks for the play-by-play. Two follow-ups: 1) add a small runbook snippet near the backend config documenting force-unlock caution, and 2) pin provider versions in staging pipeline to avoid surprise bumps.

katie: I'll add the runbook entry and make an issue to pin providers.

sara: thanks all. Marking resolved for now — will monitor for fallout in the canary deploy. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: incident-note: resolved lock zxy9-001, apply completed at 2026-03-09T09:14:59Z
